name: Nidora Course Reviews
author: nestdigitalstudio

sections.description:
Nidora Course Reviews adds student ratings and reviews to the courses you already sell with LearnPress or Tutor LMS.

It does one job. There is no page builder widget, no certificate module and no payment gateway, because every one of those belongs to your LMS and doing them badly is worse than not doing them.

What you get

  • A 1 to 5 star rating with an optional headline and a written review.
  • A per-course average, a review count, and the 1 to 5 spread as bars.
  • Stars anywhere on your site with a shortcode, including inside a course card on your course listing.
  • Structured data so Google can show stars under your course in search results.
  • A moderation screen with approve, hold, spam, trash and delete.
  • An email to you whenever a review arrives.
  • Spam defence that does not ask your students to solve a puzzle: a hidden field and a timing check, no external service, no third-party request.

Works with

  • LearnPress, free or Pro.
  • Tutor LMS, free or Pro.
  • Both at once, on the same site.
  • Any other course post type, through the crlms_course_post_types filter.

Honest about the Google stars

Review markup is a request, not a promise. Google decides whether to show stars and can stop at any time, and it ignores markup it considers self-serving. What this plugin guarantees is that the markup is valid, that it describes the page it sits on, and that it stays silent on a course with no approved reviews, which is the single most common cause of a “Rating is missing required field” error in Search Console.

What is in the paid add-on

Everything described above is free and stays free. A separate Pro add-on adds reviews restricted to students who are actually enrolled, a public instructor reply, and an automatic email asking for a review once a student finishes a course. You never need it to use this plugin.

Get the Pro add-on: https://nestdigitalstudio.com/products/nidora-course-reviews-pro

Privacy

The plugin stores what a student types, their user ID when they are logged in, and a salted one-way hash of their IP address for spam checking. The raw IP address is never stored. Nothing is sent anywhere outside your own site: no analytics, no remote fonts, no external API.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate LearnPress or Tutor LMS first, so there are courses to review.
  2. Upload the plugin through Plugins, Add New, Upload Plugin, then activate it.
  3. Open Course Reviews, Settings and check the detected LMS line at the top. It should name your LMS and your course post type.
  4. Visit a course page while logged out, or in a private window, to see the block.

The review block is added to course pages automatically. To place it yourself instead, turn off “Add to course pages” in Settings and use the [nidora_course_reviews] shortcode.
sections.faq:
Does it work with both LearnPress and Tutor LMS?

Yes, including both on the same site. Every question the plugin asks about a course goes through one adapter, so each course is handled by the rules of the LMS it belongs to.

Will my existing reviews be imported?

No. The plugin reads and writes its own table and never touches another plugin’s data, so nothing you already have is changed or lost. If you need an import from a specific plugin, open a support thread and say which one.

Can I limit reviews to students who are enrolled on the course?

That is in the Pro add-on. The free plugin can require a login and limit each student to one review per course, which stops most of the noise on a small site.

Where do the stars in Google come from?

From the structured data this plugin adds to each course page that has at least one approved review. Test it with Google’s Rich Results Test. Whether the stars appear, and for how long, is Google’s decision and nobody can promise it.

I use an SEO plugin that already adds Course markup.

Set Markup type to None in Settings, or filter crlms_schema and return an empty array. Two graphs describing the same page tend to cancel each other out.

Will it survive my theme update?

Yes. Templates are loaded from the plugin, and you can override any of them by copying the file into a nidora-course-reviews folder inside your theme, the same way WooCommerce does it. Your copy is then safe from plugin updates.

Does deleting the plugin delete my reviews?

No, not unless you tick “Delete my reviews too” in Settings first. Deactivating never deletes anything.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • The border of the review form fields is darker, so the edge of each field stands out clearly from the page (3:1 contrast or better).

1.0.2

  • The character counter under the review box now says how many characters are left, in words.
  • The review form fields get their own border, padding and focus ring, so they look the same in every theme.

1.0.1

  • The notice shown when no LMS is active now appears only on the Plugins screen and the plugin’s own screens, and can be dismissed for good.

1.0.0

  • First release.
